title: Streams Simulator Output Adapter v0.1
description: A declarative projection from the simulator's native event (sim-event-v0.1) into a consumer's wire format. Adapters are data, loaded through one path, exactly like domain specs: the binary contains no consumer-specific code, no consumer's field names, and no consumer's framing rules. Adding a consumer must never require a release.

encoding.description: Text encodings only in v0.1. Binary framings (protobuf, Sparkplug B) need a codec extension and are deliberately out of scope: a declarative adapter cannot express them, and faking it with a plugin would reintroduce consumer-specific code.

entity_id_rewrite.description: Some consumers accept a narrower identifier alphabet than the simulator's. Declare the rewrite here so it is visible and validated once, rather than discovered as a run-time rejection.

preamble.description: Records emitted once before any event — a configuration header, a schema line, a CSV header row. Rendered from run-level bindings only.

record.description: The per-event projection. It MUST carry a stable event identity derived from the native seq — either seq verbatim or a bijective encoding of it (e.g. a counter with of=seq). The duplicate and id-reuse probes, and the verdict's seq:N evidence citations, all depend on identity surviving the projection.

postamble.description: Records emitted once after the last event — an end-of-trace horizon, a terminator.

conformance.description: How to prove the adapter is correct without the consumer being present. Both are run by `streamsim adapter verify`.

output_schema.description: Path to a JSON Schema the rendered records must satisfy. Usually the consumer's published contract, vendored.

golden.description: Path to a committed expected output for the adapter conformance fixture — a fixed 12-event native trace shipped with the simulator. Byte comparison.

when.description: Optional guard. Omit the record when the condition is false — e.g. a consumer that wants no record for valueless heartbeats.

fields.description: Ordered output fields. Order is significant for csv and line encodings, and for byte-stable JSON output.

valueExpr.description: A closed set of transforms. Deliberately not an expression language: an arbitrary evaluator is a nondeterminism surface and a security surface, and every adapter written so far needs none. The same reasoning governs the F1 dynamics forms in the domain spec.

source.description: For op=source: which native event field.

fields.description: For op=object: ordered fields rendered as a nested JSON object.

template.description: For op=template: a literal with {field} placeholders naming native event fields only. No arithmetic, no conditionals, no function calls.

of.description: For op=format_time: the time-valued source to render. For op=counter: an integer-valued source (almost always seq) to render instead of the render index. Deriving the counter from seq is what keeps event identity stable across perturbation: a duplicated event keeps its id, id_reuse shows one id with two payloads, and the consumer can cite seq in its verdict. A render-order counter re-mints identity per record and silently defeats all three.

key.description: For op=run_meta: a run-level binding, available in preamble and postamble as well as per-record.
